description: Canonical registry for the future offline second-stage response-path, verifier-failure, assertion-failure, and trajectory-disposition snapshot.

selection_policy.axis_independence: Response path, verifier failure, assertion failure, policy, termination, and trajectory are independent axes; a value on one axis does not automatically determine a value on another.
selection_policy.entry_order_semantics: Every integer order field is presentation/display order only and is not classifier precedence.
selection_policy.diagnosis_selection: J2 must select the most specific diagnosis justified by retained evidence, subject to the explicit eligibility rules.
selection_policy.classifier_precedence: If classifier precedence is needed, J2 must define and test it explicitly; it must never be inferred from registry order.
selection_policy.ordinary_success_fallback: For trajectory disposition, successful_completion is the ordinary-success fallback only after checking whether positive retained evidence supports a more specific anomalous trajectory disposition.

required_manifest_bindings: input comprehensive-review manifest path and SHA-256
input trial_review.csv and trial_evidence.jsonl SHA-256 values
classifier implementation path, version, and SHA-256
output row count and output file SHA-256 values

diagnosis_object_fields.name: value
diagnosis_object_fields.description: Internal enum value from the applicable registry axis.

diagnosis_object_fields.name: label
diagnosis_object_fields.description: Friendly display label copied from the matching registry entry.

diagnosis_object_fields.name: definition
diagnosis_object_fields.description: Concise definition copied from the matching registry entry.

diagnosis_object_fields.name: confidence
diagnosis_object_fields.description: Categorical confidence; never a fabricated numeric score.

diagnosis_object_fields.name: evidence_basis
diagnosis_object_fields.description: Specific retained facts that justify the diagnosis or its conservative fallback.

diagnosis_object_fields.name: supporting_artifact_ids
diagnosis_object_fields.description: Retained artifact identifiers supporting the diagnosis; an empty array must remain explicit when no artifact ID supports the fallback.

diagnosis_object_fields.name: manual_review_required
diagnosis_object_fields.description: Whether the diagnosis requires human review under this contract.

confidence_values.label: High
confidence_values.definition: Multiple specific retained facts directly support the diagnosis with no material conflicting evidence.

confidence_values.label: Medium
confidence_values.definition: Retained evidence supports the diagnosis but is incomplete, indirect, or leaves a material alternative.

confidence_values.label: Low
confidence_values.definition: Only a conservative fallback is supportable or the retained evidence is materially incomplete.

axes.label: Response path class
axes.definition: Public derived interpretation of an invalid or empty response path, kept separate from existing activity subtype and execution-validity fields.
axes.manual_review_guidance: Specific empty-response subclasses require complete absence-sensitive evidence; use unknown when evidence cannot support or exclude a response-path diagnosis.

entries.label: Synthetic retry empty completion
entries.definition: The retained record supports an explicitly empty completion produced on the synthetic-retry response path, without attributing its cause beyond the observed path.

entries.label: Empty completion after long API-path wait
entries.definition: The retained record supports an explicitly empty completion after a prolonged observable API-path wait, without assigning provider, router, or harness fault.

entries.label: Thinking-only empty completion
entries.definition: The retained record contains observable thinking activity but no substantive completion content and an explicitly empty final result.

entries.label: Empty completion
entries.definition: The retained evidence supports an explicitly empty final completion but does not justify a more specific public response-path subclass.

entries.label: Invalid response path
entries.definition: The retained evidence supports an invalid response-path outcome but not one of the defined empty-completion subclasses.

entries.label: Unknown response path
entries.definition: The retained evidence is insufficient to determine whether a response-path diagnosis applies or which supported class is correct.

entries.label: Not applicable
entries.definition: The retained outcome does not require a response-path diagnosis.

axes.label: Verifier failure category
axes.definition: Independent public category for a verifier, task, or submitted-solution failure established by retained verifier or workspace evidence; it is not a catch-all for response-path, policy, or termination events.
axes.manual_review_guidance: Raw outcome=failure does not establish a verifier failure. Use none when no verifier/task/solution category applies, including an independently explained non-success; use unclassified_failure only after a verifier/task/solution failure is established but remains nonspecific.

entries.label: No verifier failure
entries.definition: No verifier, task, or submitted-solution failure category applies. This includes ordinary successes and non-successful trials whose retained evidence places the event entirely on another independent axis without establishing such a failure.

entries.label: Verifier environment issue
entries.definition: Retained evidence identifies a verifier or test-environment problem rather than a defect in the submitted solution.

entries.label: Syntax or compile error
entries.definition: Verifier evidence identifies syntax, parsing, type-checking, compilation, or build failure in the submitted solution.

entries.label: Dependency or import error
entries.definition: Verifier evidence identifies a missing, incompatible, or unresolved dependency, module, package, or import.

entries.label: Wrong file or path
entries.definition: Verifier evidence shows required work was placed at, read from, or written to the wrong file or path.

entries.label: Timeout inside verifier
entries.definition: Verifier-specific retained evidence shows the verifier or a verifier-invoked command exceeded its allowed time; generic termination or timeout evidence is insufficient.

entries.label: Runtime exception in solution
entries.definition: Verifier evidence identifies an exception or crash produced while executing the submitted solution.

entries.label: Test assertion failure
entries.definition: Specific retained tests or assertions ran and reported an incorrect result or behavior.

entries.label: Missing or wrong output
entries.definition: Verifier evidence identifies absent, malformed, misplaced, or otherwise incorrect required output.

entries.label: No meaningful code change
entries.definition: Positive retained workspace or verifier evidence shows that no task-relevant code change was produced.

entries.label: Partial solution
entries.definition: Retained verifier and workspace evidence shows that only part of the required solution was implemented.

entries.label: Unclassified failure
entries.definition: A verifier, task, or submitted-solution failure is established, but retained evidence does not justify a more specific primary verifier category. Raw benchmark failure alone does not establish this value.

axes.label: Assertion failure category
axes.definition: Secondary category that refines a primary test-assertion failure when retained verifier or CTRF evidence is sufficiently specific.
axes.manual_review_guidance: Use none when the primary category is not test_assertion_failure; use unclassified_assertion when an assertion failed but its retained details do not justify a specific subtype.

entries.label: No assertion failure
entries.definition: No secondary assertion category applies.

entries.label: Performance threshold failure
entries.definition: A retained assertion shows that an explicit speed, latency, memory, throughput, or resource threshold was not met.

entries.label: Numerical or data mismatch
entries.definition: A retained assertion shows incorrect numeric values, records, shapes, ordering, or other data content.

entries.label: Missing expected file or content
entries.definition: A retained assertion identifies a required file, entry, section, or content fragment that is absent.

entries.label: Behavior mismatch
entries.definition: A retained assertion shows that observed program behavior differs from the required behavior.

entries.label: Output mismatch
entries.definition: A retained assertion shows that produced output differs from the expected format or content.

entries.label: Unclassified assertion failure
entries.definition: An assertion failure is established, but retained verifier or CTRF evidence does not justify a more specific subtype.

axes.label: Trajectory disposition
axes.definition: Independent public interpretation of observable agent and workspace progress, separate from raw reward and verifier-failure category.
axes.manual_review_guidance: Use only observable retained activity and artifacts. Incomplete or nonspecific evidence falls back to indeterminate rather than a stronger narrative.

entries.label: Successful completion
entries.definition: The raw benchmark outcome is successful and retained evidence does not support a more specific anomalous trajectory disposition. This ordinary-success fallback never overrides stronger positive trajectory evidence.

entries.label: No substantive attempt
entries.definition: Complete absence-sensitive evidence shows no task-relevant implementation, tool activity, or workspace progress.

entries.label: Early abandonment
entries.definition: Observable work began but stopped before a substantive implementation attempt was developed.

entries.label: Partial implementation
entries.definition: Retained trajectory and workspace evidence shows meaningful implementation of only part of the requested behavior.

entries.label: Plausible but incorrect completion
entries.definition: The agent produced a coherent completed-looking solution, but specific retained verifier evidence shows it is materially incorrect.

entries.label: Near miss: cleanup or packaging only
entries.definition: Specific retained evidence shows the substantive solution was essentially complete and only cleanup, packaging, placement, or delivery work remained.

entries.label: Near miss: one behavioral defect
entries.definition: Specific verifier or CTRF evidence isolates one remaining behavioral defect in an otherwise substantively complete solution.

entries.label: Repeated unproductive iteration
entries.definition: Observable retained trajectory evidence shows repeated attempts that did not produce meaningful forward progress.

entries.label: Timeout after meaningful progress
entries.definition: Timeout evidence and retained substantive activity jointly show that execution ended after meaningful implementation progress.

entries.label: Completed work with verifier or infrastructure issue
entries.definition: Retained evidence supports substantively completed agent work and separately identifies a verifier or execution-environment issue.

entries.label: Indeterminate trajectory
entries.definition: Retained evidence is incomplete, conflicting, or too nonspecific to support a stronger trajectory disposition.

normalizations.reason: The public response-path taxonomy does not encode token usage in the category name.

legacy_compatibility.rule: Legacy suspect-no-op fields may remain available as stored historical heuristics, but they are not primary enum values, classifier evidence by themselves, or attribution of cause.

evidence_policy.absence_sensitive_evidence: An absence claim requires complete or otherwise explicitly adequate retained coverage for every evidence channel relevant to that claim; a missing excerpt or unavailable artifact cannot establish absence.
evidence_policy.attribution: Do not attribute a response or failure to a provider, LiteLLM, router, harness, or infrastructure component unless retained evidence specifically supports that attribution.
evidence_policy.hidden_reasoning: Hidden or private model reasoning must never be required, retained, inferred, or displayed.

eligibility_rules.requires: An explicitly empty final result, complete absence-sensitive evidence, and positive retained evidence for the named observable response path.
eligibility_rules.fallback: Use empty_completion when emptiness is supported but the specific path is not; otherwise use unknown.

eligibility_rules.requires: Complete or explicitly adequate absence-sensitive transcript, trajectory, artifact, result, and verifier evidence showing no task-relevant implementation or activity.
eligibility_rules.fallback: Use indeterminate when a relevant excerpt or artifact is missing or incomplete.

eligibility_rules.requires: Positive timeout evidence and separate retained evidence of meaningful or substantive progress.
eligibility_rules.fallback: Do not infer meaningful progress from runtime alone; use the best supported non-timeout disposition or indeterminate.

eligibility_rules.requires: Positive evidence of substantively completed agent work plus specific verifier or environment-issue evidence.
eligibility_rules.fallback: Use indeterminate or another supported trajectory disposition when either side of the conjunction is missing.

eligibility_rules.requires: Specific verifier or CTRF evidence isolating one behavioral defect and evidence that the remainder of the solution is substantively complete.
eligibility_rules.fallback: Generic failure evidence is insufficient; use plausible_but_incorrect_completion, partial_implementation, or indeterminate only when separately justified.

eligibility_rules.requires: Specific workspace and verifier evidence that substantive work is essentially complete and the remaining problem is cleanup, packaging, placement, or delivery oriented.
eligibility_rules.fallback: Use partial_implementation or indeterminate when substantive completeness is not established.

eligibility_rules.requires: Positive observable trajectory evidence of repeated attempts without meaningful forward progress.
eligibility_rules.fallback: A long runtime or high step count alone is insufficient; use indeterminate when iteration quality cannot be observed.

eligibility_rules.requires: Positive retained trajectory, workspace, result, or verifier evidence describing the extent and character of the implementation.
eligibility_rules.fallback: Raw reward=0 or raw outcome=failure alone requires indeterminate rather than either narrative.

eligibility_rules.requires: Specific retained verifier, exception, workspace, or result evidence matching the selected definition.
eligibility_rules.fallback: Use unclassified_failure only when a verifier/task/solution failure is established but specificity is inadequate. Raw outcome=failure alone does not imply unclassified_failure.

eligibility_rules.requires: No verifier/task/solution failure category applies, either for an ordinary success or because retained evidence establishes that a non-successful event belongs entirely to another independent axis without establishing such a failure.
eligibility_rules.fallback: Provider-policy refusal, invalid response path, or non-verifier timeout evidence may support none on this axis. Generic timeout evidence must not become timeout_inside_verifier without verifier-specific placement.

eligibility_rules.requires: Primary test_assertion_failure classification plus sufficiently specific retained verifier or CTRF evidence.
eligibility_rules.fallback: Use unclassified_assertion for a nonspecific assertion failure, or none when the primary category is not test_assertion_failure.

eligibility_rules.requires: A retained successful raw benchmark outcome and no positive retained evidence supporting a more specific anomalous trajectory disposition; the second-stage taxonomy does not redefine benchmark success.
eligibility_rules.fallback: When a successful trial has evidence supporting a more specific trajectory disposition, use that supported disposition instead. successful_completion is the ordinary-success fallback and must not override stronger positive trajectory evidence.
